newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Hero's welcome planned for Australian boy sailor.
newsitem.headline: Hero's welcome planned for Australian boy sailor.

text.p: An Australian teenager looked set on Friday to become the youngest person to sail solo and non-stop around the world.
Eighteen-year-old David Dicks was racing towards the Western Australian port of Fremantle, where on Sunday he is due to receive a hero's welcome, a hug from his mother -- and a truckload of mangoes.

Dicks, from the nearby city of Perth, began his epic voyage in February. Winds permitting, it should end on Sunday at 10.30 a.m. (0230 GMT) when he is expected to cross the finish line in Fremantle Harbour.

Western Australia state premier Richard Court, aboard one of thousands of boats expected to welcome Dicks home, will fire a gun to mark the occasion before customs officers board Dicks' 10-metre sloop Seaflight to stamp his passport.
Then he will be reunited with his mother Patricia, who saw him off on February 26, since when he has covered more than 50,000 kms (30,000 miles) of ocean.
"That was the hardest moment to bear to see his boat disappear over the horizon," Dicks' mother told Reuters on Friday.
"After the speeches there will be a barbecue at the Sailing Club, his first barbecue in nine months. And there will be plenty of mangoes," she added.

"When I spoke to him last I asked him what he would like most to eat and he said 'I'd love a fresh mango'. I happened to mention that on ABC (Australian) radio a few nights ago and I have had people ring me up from Kununurra and Darwin saying they were sending down crates of mangoes."
The teenager first vowed to sail around the world after another Perth yachstman, Jon Sanders, completed a similar trip when Dicks was only nine or 10.
Dicks' first attempt began on February 18 but he was back in port three days later after two of his three radios were damaged by water.
The current record for the youngest sailor to circumnavigate the globe single-handed is held by American Robert Lee Graham, who started sailing aged 16 in the 1950s.
But Graham took five years to complete the trip after stopping off to get married on the way.
